headings.title: Chapter definitions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 (subdivisions (1) to (9)) and history note (L. 1975 S.B. 170 § 1, A.L. 1989 H.B. 502, et al., A.L. 2015 H.B. 1149). Defines nine chapter-wide terms—aftercare supervision, board, child (under eighteen), commit, community based treatment, department, director, division (DYS), and youth (under twenty-one committed to DYS)—subject to the context qualification.

headings.title: Rules of number and gender construction
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. States singular/plural and masculine/feminine construction rules, expressly qualified by consistency with the intent of chapter 219.

headings.title: Division responsibilities for delinquency and rehabilitation
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1975 S.B. 170 §§ 2, 3, A.L. 1993 S.B. 52, A.L. 1995 S.B. 3). Establishes the division's overarching mandate for juvenile delinquency prevention, delinquency control, and child rehabilitation within the terms of sections 219.011 to 219.086.

headings.title: Statewide youth services program and core duties
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 (including subdivisions (1) through (9) and paragraphs (9)(a)–(b)) and history note. Covers development and administration of a statewide comprehensive youth services program, including committed-child care, the interstate compact on juveniles, statistics, evaluation, master planning, appropriated local subsidies, instructional/standard-setting materials, agency cooperation, and upon-request local and technical assistance.

headings.title: Director-assigned delinquency prevention duties
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 (including subdivisions (1) through (4)) and history note. Distinguished from subsection 2 by focusing on delinquency-prevention functions assigned by the director, including diversion planning qualified by community safety and child well-being, personnel training, interagency cooperation, and promoting effective crime-reduction programs.

headings.title: Required child, disposition, and business records
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Requires full written records of studies, examinations, conclusions, recommendations, major disposition and treatment decisions/orders for children served under sections 219.011 to 219.086, and division business transactions.

headings.title: Federal funding arrangements, contracts, and reports
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Grants permissive authority to arrange receipt of federal funds for sections 219.011 to 219.086 purposes and enter contracts or submit required federal plans and reports, qualified by consistency with this or any other act.

headings.title: Training programs for division and agency personnel
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and history note. Directs the division, pursuant to its regulations, to establish comprehensive training programs for current and prospective division employees as well as public and private agency personnel engaged in delinquency prevention and delinquent-child care and treatment.

headings.title: Training stipends, allowances, and salary continuation
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 and history note. Grants permissive authority to pay stipends, tuition, and travel/subsistence allowances and to continue salaries and benefits for division employees granted leave for approved training.

headings.title: Supplemental juvenile court services and commitment limits
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 8 and history note. Authorizes the division, upon circuit court request and by written agreement, to provide or supplement juvenile court services while keeping served children under juvenile court supervision and barring commitment without a full hearing under section 211.171(1).

headings.title: Facility revolving funds for incidental expenses
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 9 and history note. Requires the office of administration, upon division request with written department-director consent, to issue warrants up to $4,000 per facility to business managers as revolving funds for incidental expenses, subject to office of administration rules.

headings.title: Rulemaking effectiveness under section 536.024
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 10 and history note. Conditions effectiveness of any rule or portion of a rule promulgated under chapter 219 on compliance with section 536.024.

headings.title: Commitment conditions, custody limits, aftercare notice, and precare
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1975 S.B. 170 § 4 through A.L. 2025 S.B. 43). Covers commitment criteria under section 211.031(1)(2)–(3) subject to subsections 2 and 3, the age-19 custody cap (extendable to age 21 on petition and just cause), committing-court treatment plan review, three-week aftercare release notice, one-week court objection and five-working-day director response timelines, and advising the court before direct precare placement.

headings.title: Commitments involving mental or communicable diseases
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Bars commitment of children diagnosed with a mental or communicable/contagious disease, subject to a division-regulation exception when proper facility services are available and prompt mailed notice of such regulations to juvenile-jurisdiction judges and juvenile officers.

headings.title: Initial examination, placement, and maximum-security limits
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Requires prompt examination and background investigation upon commitment for placement and treatment, qualified by a bar against placing section 211.031(1)(2) commitments in maximum security facilities unless subsequently adjudicated under section 211.031(1)(3).

headings.title: Transfers to other institutions or state agencies
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Authorizes division transfers to other children's institutions after study and physical-custody transfers to another state agency when treatment is needed, requiring the receiving agency to accept the child if services are available.

headings.title: Periodic reexaminations and required reports
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Requires reexamination of committed children at least every six months, evaluating personal/family circumstances and progress, with reports sent to the committing court and parents or guardian.

headings.title: Effect of missed examinations and review petitions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and history note. Clarifies that failure to examine or timely reexamine within six months does not itself entitle a child to discharge, but entitles the child, parent, guardian, or placement agency to petition for review under section 219.051.

headings.title: Establishing, operating, and terminating facilities and programs
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 and history note. Authorizes the division, from legislatively appropriated or approved funds, to establish, build, maintain, and operate listed and other necessary facilities/programs and to terminate those no longer needed.

headings.title: Day release programs for committed children
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 8 and history note. Grants permissive authority to institute day release programs releasing committed children daily to approved local schools, public or private agencies, or persons.

headings.title: Payment efforts for section 211.185 judgments and 211.181 assessments
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 9 and history note. Requires all reasonable division efforts to ensure payment of outstanding section 211.185 judgments and section 211.181 assessments while a child is in division care, custody, or control.

headings.title: Aftercare release authority and violation actions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 (including subdivisions (1) and (2)) and history note (L. 1975 S.B. 170 § 5, A.L. 1987 S.B. 244). Subject to section 219.021(1), authorizes aftercare release, conditions, revocation, and discharge, and grants permissive authority upon substantial violation to issue hearing notice or take the child immediately into custody on danger or flight-risk grounds.

headings.title: Aftercare violation hearing procedures and venue
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Governs the subdivision (1) hearing: designated employee other than the requester presides, child/parents/guardian and counsel have full opportunity to be heard, and venue is as near as practicable to the child's "county or residence" (source wording retained verbatim).

headings.title: Rehearing requests under section 219.051
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. States permissive authority of the child or parents/guardian to request a rehearing before the director under section 219.051.

headings.title: Peace officer assistance in taking child into custody
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Requires all peace officers to assist in taking a child into custody under this section when called upon by a designated division employee.

headings.title: Law enforcement detention for alleged aftercare violations
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Requires law enforcement agencies, upon request, to detain children alleged to have violated aftercare conditions in an appropriate facility pending return and hearing, for no longer than ten days.

headings.title: Termination of aftercare supervision and written notice
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and history note. Requires terminating aftercare supervision when no longer needed or upon the child's eighteenth birthday, with immediate written notice to the child, parents or guardian, and committing court.

headings.title: Administration and appointment of division director
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1975 S.B. 170 § 6). Places division administration under a director appointed by the director of the department.

headings.title: Director residency and professional qualifications
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Requires Missouri residency while serving, broad experience and expertise in child programs, and selection based on ability, character, and integrity.

headings.title: Director oath or affirmation and surety bond
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3, history note, and Revisor footnote (*Word "of" appears in original rolls for "oath or* affirmation"). headings.title: Full-time devotion to official duties
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Requires the division director to devote full time to official duties.

headings.title: Director salary and expense reimbursement
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Provides an annual salary determined by the department director as total compensation plus reimbursement of actual and necessary official expenses.

headings.title: Merit-system hiring and applicants with prior convictions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1975 S.B. 170 § 7, A.L. 1993 S.B. 52). Requires hiring under chapter 36 subject to department-director supervision, and authorizes employing qualified persons under sections 219.011 to 219.086 despite prior criminal convictions.

headings.title: Setting employee duties and responsibilities
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Directs the division director to establish duties and responsibilities for all division employees.

headings.title: Master plan for committed-child service improvements
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Requires the director to prepare and update a master plan covering at least five years outlining structural, legislative, program, and facility changes for committed children.

headings.title: Annual progress and juvenile delinquency statistical report
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Requires an annual report describing progress on master-plan objectives and statewide and circuit-level juvenile delinquency statistics (arrests, detentions, referrals, and dispositions).

headings.title: Distribution of master plan and annual reports
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Requires transmitting the master plan and each annual report to the governor, legislature, department director, juvenile courts, and upon request to other interested persons and agencies.

headings.title: Annual statistics from state and local officials
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and history note. Requires state, county, and city officers and employees to furnish annually such statistics and information within their knowledge and control as the director deems necessary or proper under sections 219.011 to 219.086.

headings.title: Written policies, rulemaking, and public inspection
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 and history note. Requires written administration policies/procedures and necessary rules under section 219.016 and chapter 536, kept on file at the division's principal office as public records open to inspection at reasonable times.

headings.title: Service purchase contracts and constitutional limits
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 8 and history note. Authorizes contracting with qualified individuals, agencies, or institutions to purchase needed child services when more economical, effective, or practical, subject to Article I, Section 7 and Article IX, Section 8 of the Missouri Constitution.

headings.title: Federal delinquency care agreements and compensation funds
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 9 and history note. Authorizes the director as state agent to contract with federal agencies to care for delinquent children committed under 18 U.S.C. 5031–5037, with compensation deposited in the state treasury for division use upon appropriation under sections 219.011 to 219.086.

headings.title: Incentive subsidy program for local community treatment
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1975 S.B. 170 § 8). Authorizes the director to administer an incentive subsidy program assisting local units of government with community-based treatment programs for chapter 211 children.

headings.title: Eligibility rules under chapter 536 and section 219.016(6)
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Requires promulgating local eligibility rules under chapter 536 for sections 219.011 to 219.086 funds and retains verbatim the archived source cross-reference to "section 219.016, subsection 6" without silent correction (note that section 219.016(6) currently governs training programs while chapter 219 rulemaking effectiveness under section 536.024 sits in section 219.016(10)).

headings.title: County advisory committee for fund expenditure plans
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Requires the juvenile court judge to appoint an uncompensated, representative county advisory committee to participate in formulating and implementing fund expenditure plans.

headings.title: Project report and approval for county subsidy eligibility
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Requires the juvenile court judge to submit a written project report with program descriptions, implementation methods, and budgets; county subsidy eligibility follows director approval.

headings.title: Director inspections and written recommendations
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Requires the director to visit or have visited each funded program and facility to examine facilities, programs, books, and records and issue written recommendations for changes or improvements.

headings.title: Noncompliance notice, hearing, and subsidy suspension
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and history note. Upon reasonable grounds of county noncompliance with subsection 2 operating standards, requires at least thirty days' notice and a hearing on compliance progress, and permits suspending all or part of any subsidy until standards are met.

headings.title: County contracts for division services and subsidy offsets
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 and history note. Permits counties to purchase selected division services by contract under sections 219.011 to 219.086, with annual director cost determinations deducted from payable subsidies and contract costs capped at eligible subsidy amounts.

headings.title: Maintenance of county juvenile correctional spending
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 8 and history note. Bars participating counties from diminishing or reducing their juvenile correctional spending levels in order to remain eligible for subsidy of the specific subsidized program.

headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1975 S.B. 170 § 9). Sets the board's specific responsibilities under sections 219.011 to 219.086, general advisory role to the director, legislature, and public, and composition of fifteen members appointed by the department director.

headings.title: Board qualifications, partisan limits, and member terms

headings.title: Board member oath or affirmation

headings.title: Board meetings, facility visits, and written reports

Requires meeting with the director at least four times yearly to review division activities, visiting facilities as deemed necessary, and filing written reports on care, treatment, and pertinent matters with the governor, director, department director, and legislative library.

headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1997 H.B. 641 & 593 § 3). headings.title: Exemption from biennial general revenue transfer
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Exempts moneys in the Youth Services Treatment Fund at the end of any biennium from transfer to the general revenue fund under section 33.080.

headings.title: Notice and grounds for hearing petitions to director
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 (subdivisions (1) to (5)) and history note (L. 1975 S.B. 170 § 10). Requires informing committed children and their parents or guardians of the right to petition the director under promulgated rules regarding missed examinations (219.021(3) and (5)), placement decisions (219.011–219.086), and aftercare violation rehearings or custody (219.026).

headings.title: Hearing and decision timelines for petitions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Requires the director to afford an opportunity for a full and fair hearing within thirty days of receiving a petition and to render a decision within five days after the hearing concludes.

headings.title: Division authority pending petition determination
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Preserves unaffected the division's authority to act under sections 219.011 to 219.086 with respect to the child while a subsection 1 petition is pending.

headings.title: Health care standards, inspections, and deficiency reports
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1975 S.B. 170 § 11). Assigns the department of health and senior services duties to set facility health care standards, inspect buildings and sanitation, submit periodic written reports, and immediately report detrimental findings with correction deadlines to both directors.

headings.title: Educational standards, curriculum evaluations, and reports
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Assigns the department of elementary and secondary education duties to set education and attendance standards, conduct inspections and curriculum evaluations with public-school-equivalent authority, and send reports to the director, department director, and advisory board.

headings.title: Misdemeanor for aiding or concealing a runaway child
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1975 S.B. 170 § 12, A.L. 1994 S.B. 595). Makes knowingly permitting or aiding a child to run away from a division institution, or concealing the child to elude pursuit, a misdemeanor punishable as provided by law.

headings.title: Detention of runaway children by officials
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Places a duty on law enforcement officials and division-designated officials to detain a facility runaway, with or without a warrant, and hold the child subject to division orders.

headings.title: Record confidentiality, disclosures, and possible employee discharge
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Limits disclosure of committed-child records to division regulations, mandates full disclosure to parents/guardians (or out-of-state nearest immediate relative) upon reasonable notice and demand and to section 210.192 child fatality review panels, and subjects violating employees or officers to possible immediate discharge.

headings.title: Division damage actions and treasury deposit of recoveries
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Authorizes maintaining actions in the division's name for damages to the division or its real or personal property, with recoveries paid into the state treasury for division use upon appropriation.

headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1975 S.B. 170 § 13). headings.title: Authorized clinical care and religious-belief consent rules
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. headings.title: Delegated care authority of non-division residential facilities
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Limits medical, psychiatric, surgical, and dental care authority of administrators of non-division residential child caring facilities to authority delegated for particular children, subject to all limitations applicable to the division under sections 219.011 to 219.086.

headings.title: Section definition of department
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 (subdivisions (1) to (15)) and history note (L. 1995 H.B. 174, et al. § 217.598, A.L. 2015 H.B. 1149). Enumerates the fifteen state agencies and departments constituting "department" for purposes of section 219.091.

headings.title: Community work program authorization
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Grants permissive authority for DYS to establish a community work program employing committed youth in projects developed and established by any department.

headings.title: Youth selection requests and work project approval
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Permits department heads to request suitable youth for work projects and requires project design and approval by the department head and approval by the DYS director (retaining source phrasing "projects developed by the division" alongside subsection 2).

headings.title: Division custody, supervision, and work group size limit
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Retains DYS custody, supervision, and control over youth employed in work projects and caps each work group at thirteen youth.

headings.title: Work project exclusions and violent crime definition
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Bars employment in work projects of offenders convicted of a violent crime or whose conduct under DYS control suggests a propensity toward violence, and defines "violent crime" for this subsection as determined by the DYS director.

headings.title: Department duty to supply plans, tools, and equipment
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and history note. Requires the department proposing a work project to supply all necessary plans, tools, and equipment.

headings.title: Department supervisory staff and annual training
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 and history note. Requires the proposing department to supply employee staff to direct work groups and supervise project completion, with annual skill training provided by both the proposing department and DYS.

headings.title: Rulemaking under chapter 536 and section 217.040
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 8 and history note. Grants permissive rulemaking authority to the proposing department and DYS pursuant to chapter 536 and section 217.040.

headings.title: State park board authority to pay youth wages
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 9 and history note. Authorizes the state park board, out of its appropriations, to pay wages for work performed in any state park by a youth committed to the division.

headings.title: Vocational training, youth wages, and DYS trust deposits
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 10 and history note. Authorizes on-the-job vocational training and reasonable wages; declares payments property of the youth subject to division best-interest and facility-security access restrictions, and mandates deposit in the section 219.095 DYS trust fund.

headings.title: DYS Trust Fund creation, administration, and release payout
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 2015 H.B. 1149). Creates facility-level DYS Trust Funds held in financial institutions as non-state funds for youth wages and benefit moneys, credits account earnings, authorizes division regulations, exempts funds from section 33.080 general revenue transfers, and requires payout of unexpended funds upon release from DYS residential care.

headings.title: Youth fund access and money management training
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Requires a division-regulated program allowing appropriate youth access to DYS trust funds during residential care and providing training on money management, personal financial accounts, and post-discharge saving.

headings.title: DYS Child Benefits Fund for Social Security payments
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Creates the non-state DYS Child Benefits Fund in the state treasury for Social Security Administration payments, designates the state treasurer as custodian for section 30.170 and 30.180 disbursements and investments, exempts funds from section 33.080 reversion, and requires distribution upon release under federal law.

headings.title: Division service as representative payee or fiduciary
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Grants permissive authority for the division to serve as representative payee or fiduciary for Social Security or public/private benefit payments, governed by this section unless otherwise provided by law.

headings.title: Benefit deposits, accounting, and chapter 536 safeguard rules
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Requires depositing received moneys into a DYS trust fund or DYS child benefits fund, accounting in the youth's name or as representative payee, and adopting chapter 536 safeguard rules complying with federal representative-payee requirements.

headings.title: Acceptance and deposit of family or third-party funds
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and history note. Authorizes accepting funds provided by a parent, guardian, or other person for a youth's benefit, to be deposited in a DYS trust fund at the youth's residential location and governed by this section.

headings.title: Annual transaction statements for youth
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 and history note. Requires furnishing each youth annually with a statement listing all receipts and disbursements involving funds deposited with the division on the youth's behalf.

headings.title: Release or death disbursements and unclaimed-property reporting
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 8 and history note. Requires diligent prompt disbursement upon residential release or death (under descent and distribution law or federal rules for Social Security representative-payee funds) and reporting of unknown or unlocated balances under sections 447.500 to 447.595.

headings.title: Exclusion of state support and reimbursement funds
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 9 and history note. Excludes from section 219.095 funds regularly due the state for support and maintenance of youth or collected as reimbursement for state expenditures.

headings.title: Permissive grants of division facilities for compatible uses
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1996 H.B. 1117 § 1). Authorizes the director of the department of social services to grant use of DYS buildings or grounds for governmental, private, or not-for-profit activities compatible with division services.

headings.title: Notice of eligible lessees for public bid
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Requires the department director to notify the commissioner of administration which governmental, private, or not-for-profit entities may lease the buildings or grounds pursuant to public bid.

headings.title: Minimum utility and service charges for lessees
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Requires the department to charge lessees at least the cost of utilities and services furnished by the department for any leased building.

headings.title: Lease term, renewals, use conditions, and liability protection
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Limits lease terms to one year or less with optional mutual one-year renewals, requires compatible use and maintenance conditions, and mandates terms protecting the state from liability for property damages.

headings.title: Lease execution by department director
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Directs the director of the department of social services to sign the lease on behalf of the state.
